subject: Post-call: structured-output evals & model recommendations for Calliope
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Barnes <alyssa@calliope.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: structured-output evals & model recommendations for Calliope

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off a focused eval. High-level: Calliope wants reliable JSON-structured outputs from LLMs for enrichment and downstream indexing, with strict schema validation and predictable latency under 300ms 95th perc for bursty traffic.

What I heard (confirm / correct me):
- Primary use: convert short product descriptions + attributes into a validated JSON object (10 required keys; some optional arrays).
- Volume: initial pilot ~10k requests/day, potential to scale to 200k/day.
- SLOs: p95 latency target ~300ms for single-shot calls; cost sensitivity for pilot.
- Constraints: schema must be strictly enforced, retries must be idempotent, deterministic output preferred for downstream pipelines.

Immediate proposal (short):
1) Hands-on eval: Redwood will run three model variants across your prompt set and a small labelled holdout (50–100 examples) you provide. We’ll measure: schema compliance, token cost, latency distribution, and quality regressions vs. your golden set.
2) JSON validation path: run function-calling style + explicit schema enforcement. If function mode generates non-compliant output, we’ll run a lightweight repair pass (schema-driven) and surface failure rates.
3) Retries / idempotency: instrument requests with an idempotency key; on retry use deterministic decoding (greedy, temp=0) and a reduced max_tokens heuristic to avoid divergence.

Attachments I’m including: prompt set template (calliope_prompt_set_v1.csv), schema examples (calliope_schema_examples.json), and a short initial benchmarking plan PDF.

Ask from you: can you share a 50–100 item representative holdout (CSV) and confirm any fields that must never be hallucinated (PII / proprietary ids)? If helpful, Marissa (cc’d) will set up the benchmark harness and Walkthrough.

Next step: if you’re good with this plan I’ll trigger a Redwood Optimize run and schedule a 30-min calibration session next week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: structured-output evals & model recommendations for Calliope

Jonas — thanks, this is great and aligned with what we discussed. Quick answers inline: 
- We can provide a 75-example holdout (attached as sample_holdout.csv) and the full schema JSON (required fields flagged).
- Fields that must never be hallucinated: product_sku, regulatory_tag, external_id. If a field is missing, we'd prefer null rather than invented values.
- Latency: 300ms p95 is aspirational for our web flows; for async enrichment we can accept up to 1s. In the pilot we’ll surface both.

Two more asks: 
1) Can you show a short example of the retry behavior you recommend? We want predictable results if downstream retries occur.
2) Any guidance on function-calling vs. instruct-style JSON in terms of compliance and safety?

Attaching: sample_holdout.csv (small), calliope_schema_examples.json (this is the canonical schema).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the calibration session.

— Alyssa
Alyssa Barnes
Head of Integrations | Calliope.ai
alyssa@calliope.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Barnes <alyssa@calliope.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Technical plan: schema validation, model variants, and retry strategy

Thanks for sharing the holdout and schema, Alyssa. I ran a quick local pass against 10 examples to sanity-check approaches and here are pragmatic recommendations we’ll include in the benchmark run: 

Model variants to test (cost -> quality sweep):
- rw-13b-quant (cost-sensitive; fast; good baseline for structured outputs)
- rw-34b-multi (balanced: better coherence and fewer schema violations)
- rw-70b-int8 (quality-first fallback for highest compliance on edge cases)

Evaluation metrics (we’ll return per-model):
- Schema compliance rate (strict JSON schema validation using AJV-style rules)
- Repair rate (percent auto-corrected by repair pass vs. manual)
- Latency: median, p95, p99, and token-cost per call
- Determinism metric: % identical outputs on 3 repeated calls with temp=0.0

Implementation details: 
- Function-calling first: trigger function signature matching your schema so the model returns typed fields. If the function output fails validation we’ll run a single deterministic repair pass (temp=0, max_repair_tokens=50).
- Retries & idempotency: every request should include an x-request-id and an idempotency_key. If a retry occurs, server-side policy will: (a) check for an already-successful response keyed by idempotency_key; (b) if not present and network retried, resend with temp=0 and decode=greedy to minimize divergence.
- Logging & observability: we’ll capture raw model output, validation result, and repair diff in the Redwood Console under the deal RDW-8491 so you can inspect failure modes.

Quick sample configs we’ll run (will include in the bench plan):
- Variant A: rw-13b-quant | temp=0.0 | function_call=yes | max_tokens=200 | batch=8
- Variant B: rw-34b-multi | temp=0.2 | function_call=yes | max_tokens=300 | batch=4
- Variant C: rw-70b-int8 | temp=0.0 | function_call=yes | max_tokens=300 | batch=2 (fallback)

Deliverables and timeline: 
- Day 0: ingest your 75-example holdout + calliope prompt set
- Day 1: run bench suite and return a short report (compliance, cost, latency) + a link to the Redwood Console runs
- Day 2: we’ll meet for a 30-min calibration to review edge cases and agree on a rollout policy (canary thresholds, auto-fallback rules).

I’ll attach the benchmark run config and the patched prompt_set (calliope_prompt_set_v1.csv) to the HubSpot deal and share the Redwood Console link.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
